newsitem.title: DENMARK: Quiet Danish bonds sift down, set to hold levels.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Danish bonds sift down, set to hold levels.

text.p: Danish bond prices sifted marginally down in quiet holiday trade on Thursday with dealers expecting price levels to hold unchanged up to the close in a market taking a breather on top of recent gains.
"I do not see much action for the rest of the day. The market wants to stabilise after recent advances," one dealer said.

The tone-setting eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.09 point from the opening at 113.81, yielding 5,91 percent while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark 0.09 point lower at 106.55 with yield at 6.12 percent.

Turnover in the 2006 benchmark was 1,1 billion crowns, with the seven percent 2007 at only 333 million crowns. The 2006's September future fell 0.18 point to 113.08 with only one contract traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.60 point to 91.90.
The crown traded at 3.8098 per mark at 1100 gmt, down a little from around 3.8093 at the opening.
The 2007 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 56.
